title: Cancellation Safety
summary: Dropping an incomplete future cancels its operation instantly and discards its local variables.
lecture: In Rust, calling an async function or creating an async block returns a future state machine. If an executor or a select macro drops that future before it finishes, execution stops immediately at the last await point.
This behavior is called cancellation. Unlike threads or promises in other languages, cancelled Rust futures do not keep running in the background.
Any local state stored inside the cancelled future is dropped immediately. To preserve progress across cancellations, state must be stored in data structures outside the future.

example.code:
let mut buf = Vec::new();
// buf lives outside the select loop
example.caption: State stored outside the future survives cancellation.
